key_insight: EvolveNav makes zero-shot object-goal navigation improve over time at test time, instead of repeating the same mistakes. It does this by combining proactive "preflection" with a self-evolving memory that stores useful navigation rules and updates them from experience.
problem_solved: The paper addresses zero-shot object-goal navigation, where an embodied agent must find a target object without task-specific training. Existing foundation-model-based methods often depend on static priors, so they cannot adapt to new environments and tend to waste time on repeated trial-and-error.
method: Builds an agentic rule memory that extracts actionable navigation knowledge from experience.
Uses proactive preflection to anticipate likely outcomes and guide decisions before making a move.
Continuously updates memory during test time so the agent can self-improve across episodes and reduce repeated errors.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical path toward more adaptive embodied agents that learn online without retraining. It can reduce exploration cost, improve robustness in unseen environments, and make foundation-model-based navigation more reliable.
visual_elements: A before/after flow showing static-prior navigation versus self-evolving navigation.
A memory pipeline diagram highlighting rule extraction, storage, and test-time updating.
An environment map with the agent, target object, and preflection-based decision path.
An error-reduction chart showing fewer repeated mistakes over successive episodes.
paper_title: EvolveNav: Proactive Preflection and Self-Evolving Memory for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation
paper_authors: Qi Chai, Wenhao Shen, Nanjie Yao, Yue Xia, Kaiyong Zhao
